subject: Private fleet patch: contingency schedule, canary policy & rollback triggers
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tara.sheppard@edgeworks.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet patch: contingency schedule, canary policy & rollback triggers

Team / Tara —

Following last week's readiness review, I'm consolidating the contingency plan for the upcoming private-fleet patch (v4.1.2 -> v4.2.0). Goal is a 2-day narrow window with a parallel canary lane and a clearly defined rollback ladder. Key asks below — please confirm your owners and objections by EOD tomorrow.

Summary (high level):
- Version pin: customer-controlled pin at 4.1.2 for tenant nodes; we will stage a non-disruptive parallel canary group (5% of nodes) on 4.2.0.
- Maintenance window: target weekend: Sat 2026-05-30 02:00-06:00 UTC (network drains start 01:45).
- Canary cadence: two sequential slices (1% then 4%), each observed for 45 minutes of steady-state traffic prior to rollout to next slice.
- Rollback triggers: >=3% error-rate delta vs baseline, sustained CPU/latency spike (>40% increase from baseline for 15m), KV cache corruption detected, or degraded correctness on our eval set (prometheus alert INF_CANARY_EVAL_FAIL).
- Network gating: netops will hold BGP flap and tx-rate throttles until canary completes.

Open items and owners:
- Karthik: finalize canary automation in staging and add the new smoke health checks to the canary pipeline (owner: karthik_iyer).
- Ben: confirm rollback playbook steps for customer-facing tenants; ensure billing/usage doesn't double-charge during partial rollbacks (owner: ben_carter).
- Marissa: communications and SLA exception process (customer comms templates + support routing).
- Tara / EdgeWorks: confirm NOC availability and any firewall rules that must be pre-provisioned.

I've attached the draft playbook and the canary checklist (see attachments). If no major objections, we'll lock the window and create INF-9482 to track automation work.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tara.sheppard@edgeworks.com
Date: 2026-05-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch: contingency schedule, canary policy & rollback triggers

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary. I'm aligned with the proposed canary cadence but want to propose two safety additions before we lock the window:

1) KV cache snapshot & diff check: before migrating a canary slice, take a cold KV snapshot and run a diff against reference checkpoints (automated; ~6m). If diffs exceed a small delta threshold we abort that slice.

2) Rolling TLS cert validation: some on-prem clusters in EdgeWorks still have older cert chains; add a preflight step to validate TLS chains across all nodes in the 5% canary group. Failure should map to a new alert INF_CERT_WARN which will pause rollout.

I'll add both checks to the canary pipeline and open two small automation tasks under INF-9482. Accepting the weekend window but recommend we shift the first canary slice to +45m after network drain completion to allow netops to validate route convergence.

Karthik
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-05-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch: contingency schedule, canary policy & rollback triggers

Lauren / Karthik —

Good catches. A few clarifications from a customer-impact and billing perspective:

- During a partial canary rollback we need a safe path for session migration. For private tenants that rely on pinned versions, we'll surface an advisory but must provide an automated proxy-failover route that drains active requests to compatible nodes. I propose we add a temporary IP rotation (routed through the canary gateway) for the 5% group to avoid session stickiness issues.

- Billing: when we switch a tenant between pinned and staged versions there is a potential for double counting tokens if both paths are instrumented. I'll add an API flag (billing.pause_metering) we toggle for slices under test. We should document this in the playbook.

I'll prepare the rollback script snippets and update the attached playbook.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Lauren, Karthik, Ben —

Thanks for pulling this together and for the extra safety checks. EdgeWorks NOC confirms availability for the proposed weekend and will staff the bridge (lead: ops@edgeworks.com). A couple of notes from our side:

- Firewall windows: we need the CIDR list for the canary gateway by 2026-05-20 to pre-approve rules.
- Certs: we'll run a cert-chain sweep Thursday 2026-05-14 and will flag any nodes needing rotation.
- Network drain timing: we prefer the +45m offset you suggested for the first canary slice; NOC wants that buffer to watch BGP convergence across the chained racks.

We're comfortable with the rollback triggers as written. I'll mark INF-9482 in our tracker and attach our NOC runbook (referenced as EdgeWorks-NOC-Runbook.pdf locally).

Tara Sheppard
Senior Cloud Ops Manager
EdgeWorks Systems
